newsitem.title: USA: Nine alleged mobsters indicted in Florida.
newsitem.headline: Nine alleged mobsters indicted in Florida.

text.p: A federal grand jury indicted an alleged leader of the Gambino crime family and eight other alleged members and associates on racketeering charges, U.S. prosecutors announced on Wednesday.

Nicholas "Little Nick" Corozzo, of Brooklyn, N.Y., reportedly named head of the Gambino clan when reputed mob chieftain John Gotti was jailed for life, was arrested on Wednesday along with four of those indicted, prosecutors said. Warrants were outstanding for four others.
The indictment alleged that the nine ran an ongoing criminal enterprise called the South Florida Crew, a branch of the Gambino family involved in loansharking and stolen property.
Authorities said Corozzo, 56, was arrested in Key Biscayne, a posh island enclave off the coast of Miami that was the home of former President Richard Nixon's "winter White House."
Prosecutors said Corozzo was "alleged to be a ruling member of the crime family."
"This is one more step in fulfilling our mandate to target organised crime," said Miami U.S. Attorney William Keefer.

The 20-count indictment alleged the group was running a loansharking operation from a business called E-Z Check Cashing Inc. in Deerfield Beach, Fla.. Prosecutors said they will seek forfeiture of the business and $150,000 cash.

It also accused some of the defendants of trying to torch a Boynton Beach, Fla., print shop and conspiring to murder an individual suspected by the Gambino family of skimming money from its south Florida operations.

In addition to Corozzo, the indictment named Leonard DiMaria, 55, and Ralph Davino, 53, of Brooklyn; Anthony Ruggiano, 43, of Lindenwood, N.Y.; David Furman, 30, of Deerfield Beach; Sydney Alwais, 60, and David Alwais, 30, both of Boca Raton, Fla.; Salvatore Pecchio, 42, of Sunrise, Fla.; and Robert Engel, 42 of Woodhaven, N.Y.
